text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a large perf sweep after the FP8/INT8 rollout on tensor-parallel (TP) shards. Seeing 20–35% tail latency regressions on multi-GPU setups when seq_len > 512. Mostly p95/p99 spikes, not steady throughput loss.
kevin: Do you have profiler output? looks like an all-reduce bottleneck symptom to me.
sach: if you can paste the profiler dump we can check comm/compute overlap and kernel timings. even a short flame summary helps.
maria: pasted profiler snippet: 
````
run: ./bin/profiler --model rdx-3b --tp 8 --bs 4 --seq 1024 --dtype fp8 --kernels=on
summary:
  allreduce: p50=1.2ms p95=8.9ms p99=14.5ms
  attention_kernel: p50=0.6ms p95=1.1ms
  kv-shard-sync: spikes at token=0 for each new convo
  comm/compute overlap ~= 22%
````
(note: backticks intentionally single-block in slack)
jess: that kv-shard-sync line stands out — are we rebalancing shards or evicting KV on cold requests? we've seen extra rendezvous comm when cache misses happen across TP ranks.
maria: yeah, kv eviction policy triggered when prefix caching size exceeded 12MB per-rank. first token after eviction forces a sync that fans out. adds ~6–12ms occasionally.
kevin: two quick levers: 1) enable nccl async progress / UCX GPUDirect RDMA so all-reduce latency drops; 2) change kernel selector to favor compute-fused attention for long seqs so compute dominates and overlaps better with comm.
sach: concrete kernel-selector idea: "kernel_selector: auto-v2" with threshold { seq_len>=512 => fused-attn, else mem-optimized }. Also add a warmup window to avoid kernel churn on variable sequences.
jess: for batching: propose dynamic per-route batch window. example: route config: { max_batch_delay_ms: dynamic, min_batch_size: 2, max_batch_size: 32, adapt_window: 500ms } — this lets us clamp tail-latency while aggregating for throughput.
maria: tried nccl_async=true + gpudirect on the test rig: p95 dropped from 8.9ms -> ~4.5ms, avg overlap increased to ~48%. p99 still shows rare 20ms spikes correlated with kv-shard-sync.
perf-bot: scheduled perf-run job 1763123500 for maria (tp sizes [2,4,8], dtype [fp16,fp8,int8], seq [256,512,1024]). results will land in #perf-artifacts.
kevin: good. regarding INT8/FP8: did you observe numerical issues after quantization when running with TP? on paper quant scales can drift across TP partitions.
maria: yes — a few runs showed anomalous logits on ~0.2% of requests when using INT8+TP with per-shard scaling. not nan, but large deviations leading to bad completions. looks like scale mismatch across shard boundaries.
sach: we should enforce a global scaling sync for per-layer scales (one reduce-broadcast at model load or a tiny allreduce at first infer) — that will cost a tiny startup hit but avoids per-request corrections. also consider per-layer clipping thresholds for INT8.
jess: another mitigation: fall back to fp16 on layers where scale variance > threshold. kernel-selector could annotate layers with "quant-stable" flag.
maria: good idea. i'll instrument a quick check: compute per-layer scale variance across TP ranks at startup and write to /tmp/quant-stability.json. if variance > 0.1 => mark fallback.
kevin: don't forget to profile memory footprint when falling back — fp16 increases mem and may change batching behavior. run the same batch-window configs.
maria: will run the sweep that perf-bot scheduled and add the kernel-selector + quant-stability patch. plan: 1) baseline with fp16, fp8, int8 across tp [2,4,8] 2) enable nccl_async vs sync 3) toggle gpudirect 4) kv cache policy: eviction thresholds [8,12,16MB] 5) kernel thresholds seq cutoff 512/768.
sach: add nccl topology tests too (ring vs tree) — allreduce algorithm matters with NVLink vs PCIe.
devops-bot: ack: created infra test matrix and reserved A100 pool for 3 hours starting 1763129000.
maria: thanks — i'll update this thread with perf summary + concise recommendation (kernel thresholds, nccl flags, kv policy) once done. for now: priority fix = global quant scale sync + kv eviction backoff. :thumbsup:
kevin: sounds good. small follow-up: if global-sync reduces p99 only at startup, we should still look at on-the-fly rare rebalances causing mid-request spikes. maybe make rebalances epoch-based so they don't happen during inference.
jess: agreed — epoched rebalance + sticky-shard assignment for active convos.
maria: noted. adding an issue for epoched-rebalance and a short RFC for kernel-selector heuristics. will ping folks when PRs land.
